channel.title: The College Fix - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The College Fix (thecollegefix.com)

item.title: Maryland school board: We ‘expect’ teachers to use students’ preferred pronouns
item.description: The Frederick County Board of Education recently amended Policy 443 to protect gender-diverse students, requiring teachers to use students' preferred pronouns and keep updated lists. This policy allows male students identifying as female to participate in girls' sports. Critics argue it infringes on religious rights and could jeopardize federal funding, with potential litigation concerns.

item.title: Temple U. ‘pledges’ more campus cops following staffing study
item.description: Temple University plans to boost its campus police force by 58% over five years, adding 29 officers following a staffing study. This commitment aligns with President John Fry's public safety priorities. The university aims to enhance security measures and improve police-community relations amid ongoing concerns about campus safety and recent staffing challenges.

item.title: University play ‘A Gay in a Manger’ features Jesus as ‘King of Gays,’ Three Wise Men as drag queens
item.description: York St. John University staged "A Gay in a Manger," depicting a humorous retelling of the nativity with LGBTQ themes. The performance sparked controversy, prompting a complaint from a student claiming it discriminated against Christians. The university defended the play as protected artistic expression, emphasizing its commitment to inclusivity and diverse viewpoints.

item.title: Pennsylvania principal faces termination after leaving antisemitic voicemail message
item.description: Philip Leddy, principal of Lower Gwynedd Elementary, faces termination after an antisemitic voicemail meant for a student's father surfaced. The message included derogatory terms like "Jew camp" and "Jew money." Leddy, who has been principal since 2023, has been placed on leave, with a hearing scheduled regarding his dismissal.

item.title: U. Washington professor disciplined for parody land acknowledgement wins free speech suit
item.description: University of Washington professor Stuart Reges won a free speech lawsuit after being disciplined for a satirical land acknowledgement in his syllabus. The Ninth Circuit Court ruled that the university’s actions violated his First Amendment rights, emphasizing that discomfort with a professor's views should not lead to retaliation or censorship in higher education.

item.title: Georgetown responds to U.N. special rapporteurs’ claims univ. engaged in ‘human rights violations’
item.description: Georgetown University Interim President Robert Groves addressed U.N. special rapporteurs' accusations of potential human rights violations related to postdoctoral researcher Badar Suri. He emphasized the need to balance openness with legal obligations, particularly regarding immigration laws, while expressing concern for Suri's rights and free speech implications amid the ongoing discourse surrounding student activism and human rights issues.

item.title: Professor alleges Georgia college fired him for complaining about entitlement, plagiarism
item.description: Professor Adam Lamparello filed a lawsuit against Georgia College and State University after allegedly being fired for expressing concerns about student plagiarism and entitlement.

item.title: ABA accredits Catholic law school after pushback for alleged religious discrimination
item.description: A Catholic law school announced it is no longer facing a loss of accreditation after 'noncompliance' warnings from the American Bar Association.

item.title: What happened to the Christmas tree? Cornell professor makes a case for the evergreen
item.description: It's time to bring back the fresh Christmas tree.

item.title: Judge rules against UCLA prof suspended after refusing lenient grading for black students
item.description: A judge ruled against UCLA lecturer Gordon Klein, who was suspended after refusing to grade black students leniently in the wake of George Floyd's death, siding with UCLA on every issue.
